label: Chip Group
title: Chip Group
summary: Use a Chip Group to lay out a row of Chip Select filters that wraps onto new lines with even gaps.
corePrinciple: The group spaces the chips; each chip keeps its own state.

anatomy.title: Chips in a wrapping row
anatomy.description: The group holds Chip Selects in one row, 8 px apart. Chips that don’t fit move to the next line, also 8 px below.
blocks: Each chip keeps its own label, icon, and Active state.

states.title: The group has none; each chip does
states.description: Chip Group has no idle, active, or disabled state. When a chip applies, it shows its value and a close icon, grows 20 px, and the row may re-wrap.

sizing.title: Full width, 32 px rows, 8 px gaps
sizing.description: The group fills its container and adds a 32 px row for each line of chips. On the web chips are a little wider than in Figma, so Figma’s three filters need 382 px for one row.
blocks: The three filters fit on one row, with 8 px to spare.

content.title: Short filter names, then the value
content.description: Name each filter in one or two words, in sentence case. Once a filter applies, its chip shows the chosen value, so the row reads as a summary of the list.

inContext.title: Filters above a transaction list
inContext.description: The screen owns each filter: pressing an Idle chip applies it (a picker would open here), and pressing an Active chip clears it. The group only keeps the chips spaced as they change width. The screen names the row “Transaction filters”, so it is announced as a group.

sources.title: Use the public Chip Group contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Chip Group is one 370 × 32 component holding three Chip Selects in a slot, with no properties. The package wraps chips onto new rows with an 8 px gap; on the web the chips are slightly wider than in Figma, and a chip wider than the row wraps its label to stay inside it. Given an accessibility label, the row is announced as a named group; each chip is still announced as its own toggle button. The published Storybook predates the current stories, so two of its chips show no icon.
